headline: Two dead in Dhaka residential building fire; blaze controlled by 6 fire units
summary: A fire in two flats on the 12th floor of a 14-story residential building in Dhaka's Katabon area has been brought under control. Two individuals rescued from the blaze later died in hospital.
details: A fire that erupted in two flats on the 12th floor of a 14-story residential building in Dhaka's Katabon area has been brought under control. Six units of the Fire Service managed to extinguish the blaze at 3:08 AM on Friday night.

Two individuals, identified as Jony and Abdus Salam, were rescued in a burnt condition and rushed to different hospitals. Jony was taken to the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery, while Abdus Salam was admitted to Dhaka Medical College Hospital.
Tragically, both individuals were declared dead by the duty doctors at their respective hospitals. Fire Service duty officer Rafi Al Faruk confirmed these details.

The Fire Service has also confirmed that no other occupants are currently trapped inside the building, and no further casualties have been reported. The cause of the fire, however, remains unknown at this time.
caption:
Tragedy struck Dhaka's Katabon as a residential building fire claimed two lives.

A fire that erupted in two flats on the 12th floor of a 14-story residential building in Dhaka's Katabon area has been brought under control. Six units of the Fire Service managed to extinguish the blaze at 3:08 AM on Friday night.

Two individuals, identified as Jony and Abdus Salam, were rescued in a burnt condition and rushed to different hospitals. Jony was taken to the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery, while Abdus Salam was admitted to Dhaka Medical College Hospital.

Tragically, both individuals were declared dead by the duty doctors at their respective hospitals. Fire Service duty officer Rafi Al Faruk confirmed these details.

The Fire Service has also confirmed that no other occupants are currently trapped inside the building, and no further casualties have been reported. The cause of the fire, however, remains unknown at this time.

headline_marked: [[US strikes Iran]] after drone attack on cargo ship in Strait of Hormuz, peace deal questioned
headline: US strikes Iran after drone attack on cargo ship in Strait of Hormuz, peace deal questioned
summary: The retaliatory strikes by the US military on Friday followed an Iranian drone attack on a cargo vessel, raising doubts about the recently agreed interim peace deal between the two nations.
details: The US military launched strikes against Iran on Friday, responding to an Iranian drone attack on a cargo ship in the Strait of Hormuz. This action has cast uncertainty over the interim peace deal recently established between the two countries.

US Central Command reported that its aircraft targeted missile and drone storage facilities, along with coastal radar sites. Meanwhile, Iranian media indicated that a projectile struck an area near a pier in Sirik, a city situated on the strategic waterway.

Tehran has asserted its right to control the Strait of Hormuz and issued warnings to Gulf states against aligning with Washington following Thursday's attack on a cargo ship near Oman's coast. US President Donald Trump attributed the attack to Iran, stating it violated last week's agreement.

Iran had previously expressed strong disapproval of what it termed an "interventionist, irresponsible and provocative" statement by the United States and six Gulf states. This statement rejected Iran's claim that it could impose tolls on vessels transiting the strait.

Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi stated on X that "Safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz cannot be guaranteed under ambiguous arrangements, parallel routes or decision-making that does not take Iran's role as a coastal state into account."

Despite renewed questions over the strait, which typically handles a fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas supplies, oil prices dropped by about 3% on Friday. Concurrently, Saudi Aramco resumed crude loadings at its Ras Tanura terminal, the world's largest oil port, after a four-month halt.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, concluding a tour to reassure regional allies about the interim pact, issued a joint statement with the Gulf Cooperation Council. The statement called for "free, unconditional, and unrestricted navigation" in the strait, free from tolls or "attempts to assert control."

Iran's foreign ministry maintained that the strait should be governed jointly by Iran and Oman. Additionally, Ali Akbar Velayati, a top advisor to Iran's supreme leader, cautioned Washington's Gulf allies that their continued existence depended on Tehran's tolerance.
